title: Scripts: retrieval evaluation & failure analysis
purpose: This subsystem is the evaluation and QA harness for the RAG pipeline. It runs benchmark questions (loaded from evaluation/questions.yaml plus hardcoded regression sets) through the live /chat stack under baseline and optimized configurations, measures latency, recall, confidence, and correctness, classifies answers into four quality categories, diagnoses failed questions down to the retrieval/rerank/LLM stages, and generates Markdown/JSON comparison and timing reports. It also fabricates synthetic real-world datasets for retrieval robustness testing and serves as the project's verification gate (verify_project.py, referenced from CLAUDE.md). The scripts are the evidence base that drove retrieval tuning decisions such as RRF weight adjustment, canonical source boosting, and top-k reduction.

data_flow: Most scripts are standalone CLI tools that run from the repo root using cwd-relative paths. compare_baseline_vs_optimized.py is the central producer: it builds two RAGChatService instances (via src imports of create_rag_pipeline / create_llm_service) and writes evaluation/results/baseline_vs_optimized_comparison.json. The downstream consumers — analyze_all_failures.py, export_all_21_failures.py, audit_evaluation_4_categories.py, fresh_audit.py, generate_comparison_report.py, deep_diagnose_21_failures.py, diagnose_each_failure.py, inspect_dep001.py, inspect_remaining_3_incorrect.py — read that JSON (plus evaluation/questions.yaml for expected keywords/sources) and produce further artifacts in evaluation/results/ (failed_questions_analysis.json, all_21_failures_full.json, audited_4_category_benchmark.json, full_comparison_report.md). Pipeline-exercising scripts (compare_baseline_vs_optimized.py, diagnose_retrieval_failures.py, measure_baseline_timing.py, test_retrieval.py, test_retrieval_tuning.py, test_pipeline_timing.py, verify_rag_queries.py) import from src/ and call RAGChatService.respond / create_rag_pipeline / create_llm_service, which requires a live Ollama server, a loaded FAISS index, and the local sentence-transformer embedding model; measure_baseline_timing.py writes per-stage timings to logs/. benchmark.py delegates to the evaluation/benchmarks package (RetrievalBenchmark -> RetrievalPlotter -> RetrievalReportGenerator), writing reports under evaluation/reports/. The dataset generators (generate_full_evaluation_dataset.py, generate_real_world_dataset.py) write evaluation/datasets/real_world.yaml. verify_project.py shells out to pytest, ruff, and coverage, writing its JSON verification report to data/analytics/reports/.
external_deps: PyYAML (yaml.safe_load / yaml.safe_dump) — all dataset and questions.yaml readers/writers
pytest + pytest-cov (invoked via subprocess by verify_project.py)

FAISS vector index via src FAISSSimilarityStore (compare_baseline_vs_optimized.py, diagnose_retrieval_failures.py, measure_baseline_timing.py, test_retrieval.py, test_retrieval_tuning.py, test_pipeline_timing.py)
Ollama LLM service via src (live server required for any script that calls respond/generate)
Standard library: json, argparse, hashlib, subprocess, time, tracemalloc, pathlib
risks: Hardcoded cwd-relative paths (evaluation/..., data/..., logs/...) — the scripts only behave correctly when run from the repo root; several silently no-op if their input JSON is absent.

benchmark.py contains dead, broken dry-run wiring that references the undefined name benchmark_engine_mock_adapter (survives only because a `if False` ternary short-circuits to None); the advertised mock-adapter dry-run mode is non-functional.

compare_baseline_vs_optimized.py constructs Settings objects explicitly, bypassing the config.yaml/.env precedence rules, so baseline/optimized results can silently diverge from the production configuration (config-drift risk flagged in CLAUDE.md).

Correctness/refusal/hallucination classification is heuristic throughout: substring keyword coverage plus hardcoded refusal-phrase lists and URL domain whitelists — prone to misclassification and overfitting to the 35-question benchmark.

Fragile introspection of private pipeline internals (pipeline._similarity_store, ._reranker, hybrid.bm25_store, hybrid._bm25_indexed) and runtime monkey-patching of instance methods (measure_baseline_timing.py) — breaks on any internal refactor.
test_retrieval.py builds embeddings/FAISS/loader/chunker objects it never uses, then re-creates everything through the factory — dead construction and duplicated config wiring.
test_retrieval_tuning.py re-implements the entire RRF fusion loop by hand instead of calling hybrid_retriever.search — a drift-prone copy of production logic.

generate_full_evaluation_dataset.py and generate_real_world_dataset.py are near-duplicates both writing evaluation/datasets/real_world.yaml with empty expected_answer/expected_citations placeholders; running one silently overwrites the other.
verify_rag_queries.py hardcodes a single refusal string and special-cases 'Where is Block 7?', so its PASS/FAIL verdicts are tuned to that specific interaction text.
Minor hygiene issues: fresh_audit.py opens files without explicit encoding; inspect_dep001.py executes at import time; benchmark_conversation_memory.py's <10ms latency assertion is potentially flaky.
These scripts are standalone tooling not collected by pytest, so regressions in the evaluation harness itself are not caught by the CI/verify gate.
